summary: Implemented individual root placement in Windows browse using existing work. The row menu opens a Kit destination dialog after a fresh authorized read and saves only the group field through move_group_item; failure review preserves the requested destination ID and separates reading from explicit Apply. Group-local grips reuse boardcraft-ui's threshold/edge controller and submit one anchor command to reorder_group_item. Both narrow native HTTP contracts enforce current selected Member/Owner write access in the existing host transaction. Accepted rows remain visible through commit and confirmation, uncertain recovery never repeats a command automatically, and toolbar batch append remains independent. Reused the compared packet 33/34 records, native selection fixture, whole-record snapshot oracle, relay and desktop controls. Documentation adds only the affected Windows workflow row and this handoff. Pre-existing roadmap, runner and packet edits were preserved.
evidence: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke windows_moves_and_reorders_single_roots -- --exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture: passed. Running GPUI windows selected the other Work by ID, cancelled without writing, then moved 61 before 59 without changing its position, creation provenance, position stamp or board revision. On the separate reorder fixture, grip drops produced [73,67,61,77] then [73,61,67,77], with dense positions, board revisions 2/3, selected item revisions and both stamps 2/3, and distinct receipts. Parent connections independently checked all stored records, accepted grouped reads and HTTP bodies/statuses/counts. Both accepted results survived a new visit and a fresh desktop process with no replay.

The same Windows success check passed subthreshold (3,4) travel versus exact six-pixel activation, exact row midpoint versus one pixel below using the rendered hairline, Escape, self/outside/cross-group/already-adjacent releases, subsequent working name editing and cancellation, retained group-entry draft and ID-bound selection. A fixture board lock kept each save pending: controls were disabled, accepted order remained visible, and repeat Confirm plus a second otherwise-valid grip drop did not submit another command.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke windows_recovers_single_root_placement -- --exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture: passed all 14 modes. Each command covered a peer revision conflict, deferred commit refusal, Member demotion to Viewer, membership denial, revoked session, lost successful acknowledgment and failed post-commit confirmation read. Independent whole-store readbacks ran before recovery and before fault removal. Review/reload sent reads only; explicit Apply or a new deliberate drop/action submitted separately using fresh baselines. An acknowledged-but-unconfirmed menu move followed by Apply remained a same-group no-op, unlike a fresh reverse reorder. Lost confirmations also covered another refused recovery read and its successful retry, with no intervening write.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --test loopback_board_access native_single_root_placement_checks_access -- --exact --nocapture: passed on real HTTP. Both routes checked method/route isolation, direct/scoped refusal, missing/revoked bearer, current Viewer/Member/Owner, workspace membership, board subscription and active catalog state; invalid/foreign/inactive item, group and anchor scopes; malformed/nonpositive/future inputs; and deferred rollback. Reorder replay still required current access, changed receipt content conflicted, an anchor moved since read conflicted, and the old group baseline could not cross a reorder. A menu move crossed a name-only revision, preserved the accepted spelling and storage keys, and left positions, board revision and receipts unchanged. Current same-group no-op and stale group-baseline rejection were checked separately.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-ui --lib: 3 passed. Includes grip-only start geometry, logical threshold, whole-row midpoint, release-position edge calculation without activating a short click, cancellation, outside-viewport cleanup and inherited heading scroll/generation behavior.

Focused inherited Windows checks passed individually with cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke <name> -- --exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture: windows_reorders_physical_groups, windows_moves_selected_roots_to_group, windows_creates_and_renames_grouped_root. Heading drags, distinct toolbar append, selection and editable names remain working.
cargo clippy --locked -p boardcraft-desktop -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host -p boardcraft-ui --features boardcraft-desktop/native-smoke --all-targets -- -D warnings: passed on final sources.

cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check: passed. Diff statistics and new-file scope were reviewed; this is a small packet, below the change-size ceiling. No commits, pushes, verification markers, runner gates or process-document edits were made by this worker.

Initial compound environment/status commands were denied, but standalone Cargo used the inherited dedicated test environment successfully. Early compile errors and driver query/retry failures were corrected before the passing focused runs. Full inherited suites, workspace tests, runner verification, browser/Android journeys and attended clipboard checks were intentionally not run. Native drivers dispatch GPUI pointer/keyboard events and inspect rendered controls/geometry, not physical-device input or pixel fidelity. Physical capture-loss, theme/zoom/translation sweeps, touch, row auto-scroll and cross-group dragging remain unverified or out of scope. Failed move requests and drafts remain visit-local, as in the compared workflows.
